sources: Turkish Presidency Directorate of Communications (Burhanettin Duran, X post, Oct 30); confirmed by Zelenskyy (Kyiv Independent update Oct 30)
fault_line: Mediator or bystander: can Turkiye actually stop Black Sea ship strikes, or is Istanbul just another photo-op while both sides keep shooting at ships?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- visit + agenda] Volodymyr Zelenskyy pays a working visit to Turkiye on Saturday Oct 31 at Recep Tayyip Erdogan's invitation; Istanbul talks cover bilateral cooperation, the Russia-Ukraine war and Black Sea security, per Duran: 'the meetings in Istanbul will cover steps to further strengthen cooperation between Turkiye and Ukraine, as well as regional and international developments, particularly the Russia-Ukraine war and the security situation in the Black Sea.' Erdogan hosts at his Dolmabahce office, followed by a news conference (Turkish presidency via Turkiye Today). Zelenskyy called the talks 'an important part of efforts to end the war' in his Friday video address, with further discussions expected in November. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Clash Report: the announcement names no agreement scheduled for signing and does not describe the visit as a new round of peace negotiations. Context: Erdogan spoke to Putin in early October on Black Sea security; Ankara has put forward a draft agreement to halt attacks on civilian vessels, on which 'the two foes have failed to act' (Arab News Oct 30); Turkish Defence Minister Yasar Guler warned Oct 28 Ankara reserved the right to take legal action if Turkish-flagged/owned vessels are attacked. Zelenskyy said Oct 28 in The Hague he hopes for an Abu Dhabi meeting Nov 6-10 (Clash Report).

sections.what_disputed: Clash Report: no agreement scheduled for signing; not a new peace-negotiation round. Mezha/Radio Svoboda initially noted Ukraine had not yet confirmed the visit (later confirmed by Zelenskyy per Kyiv Independent). No outcome exists yet -- the visit is process until the news conference produces a measure or date.
